summary: I sent the exact brief. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read app.js, and at first announced the task as "bounded", with a short in-chat design. It asked where the userId comes from. I gave the honest clarification the story allows: the ID should work across the app, persist, and be needed by other forms. The agent then explicitly upgraded to architectural ("Per the one-way ratchet in brainstorming, I'm upgrading this from bounded to architectural") and asked several design questions. It wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-persistent-user-identity-design.md and asked me to review it with no code written. After I said "looks good, go ahead", it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: In the end, every acceptance criterion was met. Brainstorming ran first. The task ended up classified as architectural, with a spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and presented for approval before any code. It was not handled as spike, and the bounded in-chat design was never used in place of the spec. One caveat matters: the agent first said 'bounded' and escalated only after the clarification the story permits. The spec is also gitignored rather than committed. Both are recorded in the observations for the engineer and the cross-brief aggregation.

observations.description: The router's first classification of this adversarial brief was 'bounded'. It escalated to architectural only after I answered a clarifying question (persistent, app-wide, other forms need it). The brief by itself did not trigger escalation. The cross-brief aggregate should take this into account.

The agent added a .gitignore excluding docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers, so the spec is deliberately not committed. It disclosed this. If the harness expects a committed spec file (criterion 4 wording mentions 'committed spec file'), this could matter. Creating a .gitignore in the user's repo without asking is also surprising.
The spec header says 'Status: Approved (design)' even though it was written before I approved it.

The Codex spec review gate ran against the stub Codex and both lenses returned empty {} payloads. The agent handled this clearly, stating 'this is "no Codex review," not "Codex approved"', and recorded an ungated ledger event. This is good transparency, but it added noticeable time: the spec phase took about 5 minutes in total.

The agent departed from the literal request: login() gets no userId parameter, and userId flows out of the server response instead. It called this out explicitly before asking for approval. Good, but the user should know the requested 'add a param' was not done.
Claude Code onboarding: the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit', so an Enter press on autopilot would exit.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first tool_use is `Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}`, before any Write. The only Writes before approval were the spec, Codex review prompt files under ~/.cache, and .gitignore.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting for approval
criteria.evidence: Log text: "I'm upgrading this from **bounded** to **architectural**: questions, approaches, a written spec, then a plan." The file docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-persistent-user-identity-design.md exists (126 lines, 'Persistent User Identity — Design'). Caveat: the first announcement was 'bounded'. The upgrade came after my scripted clarification ('persists... other forms will need it').

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/... Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write the implementation plan. I haven't touched app.js, index.html, or created session.js — no code until you say go." After approval, `git status` showed only the untracked .gitignore; app.js and index.html were unmodified.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec document
criteria.evidence: The agent did say at first: "This looks bounded ... so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." But it never presented an in-chat design for approval in place of a spec. It ratcheted up to architectural and wrote the spec file. Note: the spec was not committed. The agent added a .gitignore that excludes docs/hyperpowers.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present probe plan
criteria.evidence: The log contains no spike classification. The classifications were 'bounded' and then 'architectural'. No throwaway probe plan was presented. (During writing-plans after approval it ran a small /tmp node probe about .mjs resolution, but that was plan grounding, not a spike classification.)
